rules: Regular election for a full term (2027-2033); the appointed senator serves until the term ends on January 3, 2027. Plurality winner in the general election (runoffs apply only to primaries). Four candidates: Darline Graham (R), Annie Andrews (D), Kasie Whitener (Libertarian), Mark Hackett (Constitution). Write-in votes are allowed; Catherine Fleming Bruce is running as a write-in candidate. Early voting ran October 19-31, 2026; absentee ballots must be returned by 7 p.m. on November 3. South Carolina has no party registration. Polls close at 7 p.m. Eastern; results are usually reported on election night. Sources: https://scvotes.gov/early-voting-ends-saturday-reminders-for-election-day-november-3/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_election_in_South_Carolina

candidates.name: Darline Graham
candidates.current_or_last_office: U.S. senator (appointed; in office since July 14, 2026)
candidates.bio_short: Graham, the sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, was commissioner of the South Carolina Commission for the Blind (2019-2026) before Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to the seat in July 2026. She is the first woman to represent South Carolina in the U.S. Senate.
candidates.primary_result: Won the August 11, 2026 special Republican primary with 32.8% (109,881 votes; first of 10 candidates), then the August 25 runoff against U.S. Rep. Ralph Norman, 52.4% (193,486 votes) to 47.6%.

candidates.name: Annie Andrews
candidates.current_or_last_office: Pediatrician; former professor of pediatrics at the Medical University of South Carolina
candidates.bio_short: Andrews is a pediatrician who was the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 1st congressional district in 2022, losing to Rep. Nancy Mace. She won the Democratic Senate nomination in June 2026, when the Republican nominee was still Lindsey Graham.
candidates.primary_result: Won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 61.5% (226,075 votes) over Brandon Brown (30.2%) and Kyle Freeman (8.3%).

candidates.name: Kasie Whitener
candidates.current_or_last_office: Former chair of the South Carolina Libertarian Party State Committee
candidates.bio_short: Whitener is the Libertarian nominee and took part in the October 11 televised debate. Her FEC committee reported $27,615 raised through October 14, 2026.
candidates.primary_result: Libertarian nominee (chosen at the party convention).

candidates.name: Mark Hackett
candidates.bio_short: Hackett is the Constitution Party nominee; Wikipedia lists him as a house painter. No FEC financial summary was found for him.
candidates.primary_result: Constitution Party nominee (chosen at the party convention).

candidates.name: Catherine Fleming Bruce
candidates.current_or_last_office: Author; candidate in the 2022 Democratic Senate primary
candidates.bio_short: Fleming Bruce did not file for the 2026 primary and is running a write-in campaign in the general election, per Wikipedia. Her name is not printed on the ballot.
candidates.primary_result: Did not run in the primary (write-in candidate).

events.what: Initial primaries: Sen. Lindsey Graham won the Republican primary with 56.8%; Annie Andrews won the Democratic primary with 61.5%.
Gov. Henry McMaster selected Darline Graham, Lindsey Graham's sister, for the seat after President Trump and Majority Leader John Thune recommended her; she was sworn in on July 14.
Trump endorsed Darline Graham for the Republican nomination.
Darline Graham announced she would run in the special Republican primary.
A Richland County judge ordered Danny Ford II onto the special primary ballot after the state GOP disqualified him under a new party rule.
Special Republican primary: Darline Graham 32.8%, Ralph Norman 24.6%, Russell Fry 19.7%, Mark Sanford 14.9%; no candidate won a majority.
Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg endorsed Andrews, The Post and Courier reported.
Runoff: Darline Graham defeated Ralph Norman 52.4% to 47.6%.
Rep. Ralph Norman, the runoff runner-up, endorsed Graham, The Hill reported.
Graham agreed to debate Andrews, WBTV reported; Andrews had been publicly challenging her to debate.
Graham, Andrews and Libertarian Kasie Whitener met in a one-hour debate at SCETV in Columbia, the only debate both major candidates had committed to.
Former Republican state Sen. Katrina Shealy endorsed Andrews, The State reported.
The State Election Commission reported nearly 564,000 early ballots, a record for a gubernatorial-year (midterm) election.
The National Rifle Association endorsed Graham, WIS reported.

early_vote.summary: South Carolina Election Commission: nearly 564,000 ballots cast during early voting as of 3 p.m. Oct. 26, above the previous gubernatorial-year record of 561,563 (2022); the all-time record is 1,471,663 (2024). Early voting continued through Oct. 31. South Carolina has no party registration, so no partisan breakdown exists.

notes_uncertain: WTOC reported 671,314 early votes through Oct. 27, citing commission data (https://www.wtoc.com/2026/10/28/over-600k-votes-cast-sc-sees-record-early-voting-turnout/); not checked on scvotes.gov.
Annie Andrews' exact birth date not found (Wikipedia: born 1981), so age is null (44 or 45).
Wikipedia poll footnotes spell the Libertarian 'Kasie Whitner'; the ballot name is Kasie Whitener. Footnotes are copied as written.
Lindsey Graham's former campaign committee (S0SC00149) is listed under money.other_committees; how its remaining funds were used after his death was not verified.
Mark Hackett: no FEC financial summary found.

Wikipedia mentions a 'write-in Ralph Norman' effort by some Republican voters (citing an MS NOW blog post, Sept. 2, 2026); its scale was not verified, and Norman endorsed Graham the same day (The Hill).
Ages are as of Election Day (2026-11-03), computed from birth dates on the candidates' Wikipedia pages.
